title: Rajinikanth Marks 51 Years in Cinema as Dharman Shoot Progresses in Chennai
excerpt: The superstar's career milestone coincides with India's Independence Day — the same date his debut film Apoorva Raagangal released in 1975 — as he films his 173rd movie produced by Kamal Haasan.
body:
• August 15, 2026 marks 51 years since Rajinikanth's debut in K. Balachander's Apoorva Raagangal, which released on India's Independence Day in 1975.
  • Rajinikanth is currently filming Dharman, his 173rd film, in which he plays a doctor for the first time in his career — directed by Ashwath Marimuthu and produced by Kamal Haasan.
  • The film marks the first producer-actor collaboration between Kamal Haasan and Rajinikanth, two icons who have shared a friendship spanning over five decades.
  • Dharman co-stars Simran, Raashii Khanna, and Yogi Babu, with music by Anirudh Ravichander, and is targeting a Pongal 2027 release.

Superstar Rajinikanth marks 51 years in Indian cinema on August 15, 2026 — the same date his debut film, K. Balachander's Apoorva Raagangal, released on India's Independence Day in 1975. The milestone finds him on the sets of Dharman in Chennai, his 173rd film and the latest chapter in a career that has made him one of the most celebrated figures in Indian film history.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=0-1nXO4gVNM

Rajinikanth first appeared on screen alongside Kamal Haasan in Apoorva Raagangal in a minor role, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. In the five decades since, he has acted in more than 165 films across Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, and other languages, earning the title "revenue king" of Indian cinema and the devotion of fans who refer to him simply as "Thalaivar" (The Leader), IANS reported.

Dharman: A Historic Collaboration

Dharman brings together Rajinikanth and Kamal Haasan in their first-ever producer-actor collaboration. Produced by Haasan and R. Mahendran under Raaj Kamal Films International (RKFI), the film is directed by Ashwath Marimuthu, known for Oh My Kadavule and Dragon, according to Bollywood Hungama.

The first-look poster, unveiled on June 24 when principal photography commenced, presents Rajinikanth in blue surgical scrubs and sunglasses, holding a blood-stained scalpel inside an operation theatre. It marks the first time in his career that Rajinikanth is playing a doctor, with the tagline "The Deadly Doctor," per Bollywood Hungama.

"Dharman is not about the Rs 5 doctor. This is about a swaggy and deadly doctor called Dharman. It'll be a very entertaining, family-oriented thriller."

— Ashwath Marimuthu, director

At the title announcement event, Haasan shared the title poster on social media with the line "Dharmame vellum!" (Dharma will prevail), formally introducing the project that had been promoted under its working name Thalaivar 173, according to Cinema Express.

A Turbulent Path to Production

Dharman has seen significant directorial changes since it was first announced. Sundar C was initially attached but stepped away, later revealing he left due to "feeling pressured," per the film's Wikipedia entry. Cibi Chakravarthy then came on board and worked through pre-production before departing as well. Ashwath Marimuthu was confirmed as the third director after both Rajinikanth and Haasan were impressed with his script, Bollywood Hungama reported.

The supporting cast includes Simran, who reunites with Rajinikanth after Petta (2019), Raashii Khanna, and Yogi Babu, in his fourth collaboration with the superstar. Music is composed by Anirudh Ravichander, with action sequences choreographed by the National Award-winning duo Anbariv, according to Koimoi.

A Year of Milestones

Rajinikanth's 50th anniversary last year was marked by the release of Coolie, directed by Lokesh Kanagaraj, and a Lifetime Achievement Award at the 56th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in November 2025. At the ceremony, attended by his family, Rajinikanth reflected on his journey. "50 years of acting in cinema felt like 10 or 15 years. If there are 100 more janams (lives), I would like to be born again as an actor and as Rajinikanth," he said, according to The Hollywood Reporter India.

What's Next

Dharman is targeting a Pongal 2027 theatrical release, with Red Giant Movies handling distribution, per Bollywood Hungama. Rajinikanth also has Jailer 2, directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, in his pipeline. At 75, the superstar shows no signs of slowing down — continuing to set benchmarks in an industry he helped define.
nri_angle: Rajinikanth remains a cultural icon across the Indian diaspora worldwide, with his films drawing massive opening-day crowds at theaters in the US, UK, and other countries with significant Indian populations.
